prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S137: Shift Commander sends the Mutual Aid Release Form when a neighboring service is released from regional coverage.
S138: Regional Dispatch Center uses the swap voucher to confirm that a unit's battery readiness is current before it is placed in service.
S139: Regional Dispatch Center uses the queue snapshot to account for congestion approaching the northern entry before assigning a route.
S140: North Gate Status Board displays the latest queue condition and access restriction for units approaching the northern entry.
S141: Triage Supervisor advises dispatch when changes in clinical demand may require repositioning available units.
S142: Regional Medical Director establishes clinical priorities that dispatch applies when assigning units during elevated demand.
S143: Hospital Liaison Desk provides receiving-facility capacity information for consideration during transport planning.
S144: Dispatchers compare projected response times with remaining coverage before moving a unit away from its current area.
S145: Data Quality Officer reviews inconsistent location or status reports and routes corrections through the established operational process.
S146: Ambulance Coordination Platform retains time-stamped status changes so supervisors can review the sequence of unit movement.
S147: A crew advises dispatch when a road closure, unsafe condition, or unexpected delay makes the assigned route unsuitable.
S148: Regional Dispatch Center records the approved alternative route and checks that the change does not leave a critical area without reasonable coverage.
S149: The Hospital Liaison Desk coordinates destination consultation when a patient’s condition or the operating status of a facility may affect the assignment.
S150: The consultation uses the patient’s reported condition, transport estimate, and current facility acceptance information available to the Regional Dispatch Center.
S151: The Regional Medical Director provides clinical guidance when destination selection involves a specialized capability or a regional care protocol.
S152: The Hospital Liaison Desk contacts the Emergency Department to confirm whether the proposed destination can receive the patient.
S153: The Regional Dispatch Center uses the correction slip to reconcile a reported destination change with the active incident record.
S154: Larkspur confirms the incident identifier and intended receiving facility before the destination request is transmitted.
S155: The Emergency Department advises the Hospital Liaison Desk of relevant capacity limits, access constraints, or changes to its receiving status.
S156: The Hospital Liaison Desk records the consultation outcome and communicates any destination restriction to the Regional Dispatch Center.
S157: The Regional Dispatch Center evaluates the consultation outcome against patient acuity, transport time, and available ambulance coverage.
S158: The Ambulance Coordination Platform presents the approved destination and any associated operational instructions to dispatch staff.
